import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# $a(n) = 3a(n-1) + a(n-2) - 3a(n-3)$

*References:*
- [A103425](https://oeis.org/A103425)
-/

namespace OeisA103425

/--
The primary defining sequence `a`.
$a(n)$ is defined by the recurrence relation $a(n) = 3 a(n-1) + a(n-2) - 3 a(n-3)$
with initial terms $a(0)=1, a(1)=3, a(2)=5$.
-/
def a : ℕ → ℕ
  | 0 => 1
  | 1 => 3
  | 2 => 5
  | n + 3 => 3 * a (n + 2) + a (n + 1) - 3 * a n

/-- Term theorems verifying the first few values of the sequence against the official OEIS b-file -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_0 : a 0 = 1 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 3 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 5 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 15 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 41 := by decide

def IsWeightedTribonacci (a b c : ℤ) (x : ℕ → ℤ) : Prop :=
  ∀ n, x (n + 3) = a * x (n + 2) + b * x (n + 1) + c * x n

/--
The current sequence contains primes, including $3, 5, 41, 21523361$.
Is there an $(a, b, c)$ weighted tribonacci sequence with $a, b, c$ relatively prime
which is prime-free?
-/

@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (a b c : ℤ) (x : ℕ → ℤ),
      Nat.gcd (Int.gcd a b) c.natAbs = 1 ∧
      IsWeightedTribonacci a b c x ∧
      ∀ n, ¬ (x n).natAbs.Prime := by
  sorry

end OeisA103425

findings.description: The existentially quantified sequence has unrestricted initial values: IsWeightedTribonacci imposes only the recurrence. Consequently, a = b = c = 1 and x ≡ 0 satisfy the entire right-hand side. I proved this, and the exact answer(True) formulation, without sorry in /workspace/review/scratch.lean. Even requiring positive terms would not suffice: x ≡ 4 works with coefficients (3, 1, -3). This warrants clarification of the intended admissible sequences. It is not a confirmed omitted hypothesis, however: the cited OEIS comment itself leaves initial values and nondegeneracy unspecified, and its linked references do not establish a general restriction.
findings.source_evidence: Jonathan Vos Post's comment in OEIS A103425, Feb 05 2005, asks: “Is there an (a, b, c) weighted tribonacci sequence with a, b, c relatively prime which is prime-free?” It then gives the general third-order recurrence, without conditions on initial values. Read through https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A103/A103425.seq. The referenced A102001 and its companion A102002 use the same weights with different initial values; MathWorld's linked Linear Recurrence Equation article likewise does not prescribe a normalization.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify from the source whether any initial-value or nondegeneracy restrictions are intended, and encode those restrictions if so; the available references do not justify a specific stronger statement. If unrestricted initial values are intended, retain the mathematical statement, supply answer(True) and the elementary zero-sequence proof, and classify it accordingly rather than as a nontrivial open question.

reformulations.difference: The definition uses ℕ and truncated subtraction, whereas the source presents an ordinary integer recurrence.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The subtraction never truncates. In /workspace/review/sequence_checks.lean I proved a n ≤ a (n + 1), hence 3 * a n ≤ 3 * a (n + 2) + a (n + 1). Casting a into ℤ therefore gives exactly the source recurrence. The sorry-free theorem source_recurrence_iff proves that an integer sequence equals this cast precisely when it has initial values 1, 3, 5 and satisfies the source recurrence. I also proved the source's closed formula in the equivalent form 2*a(n) = 3^n + 2 - (-1)^n.

sources_consulted: OEIS A103425, full entry including Jonathan Vos Post's question: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A103/A103425.seq
could_not_verify: OeisA103425.conjecture: the literal unrestricted reading is verified and trivially true, but the cited sources do not determine whether a more restrictive, nontrivial prime-avoidance problem was intended. Thus I cannot substantiate a definite missing mathematical hypothesis.
review.notes: All eight declarations were reviewed. The five term theorems agree with the source; evaluation also matched all 27 listed terms and verified primality of 3, 5, 41, and 21523361. The answer placeholder has the correct propositional scope. Int.gcd, Nat.gcd, Int.natAbs, and Nat.Prime were inspected and tested at boundary values. No source-recorded resolution was found, so the elementary witness is not presented as a source-backed status update. OEIS's main pages were blocked by Cloudflare; the full entries were read through the OEIS data repository instead. The reviewed file's blob matches the specified commit.
